A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZIM and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Their contents can be reliably matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original MicroMat-3K evaluations, component and hyperparameter ablations, and inpainting, medical segmentation, and 3D segmentation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds training-dataset controls, downstream comparisons, prompt-count experiments, and transparency evaluation.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same label converter, augmentation and selective learning strategies, losses, hierarchical decoder, and prompt-aware attention. Added fine-tuning and component-transfer experiments do not establish a revised ZIM algorithm. Text and scribble prompting already appear in v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds dedicated transparent-object matting on Transparent-460 and fine-grained segmentation transfer on DIS, COIFT, HRSOD, and ThinObject. These extend the evaluated tasks and data coverage. The original MicroMat-3K, automatic-mask-generation, inpainting, medical, and 3D scenarios remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds GFM and AIM to traditional matting comparisons, IndexNet, MGMatting, and TransMatting to transparency comparisons, and Matte-Any and Matting-Any to downstream comparisons. Table 1 removes SAM2 and SMat, although both remain in appendix Table 6. Table 8 also introduces component-augmented comparison variants.

E3.justification: New evaluations sweep 2–10 point prompts, swap training datasets, test 1% versus 10% training data, and fine-tune ZIM on Transparent-460 while comparing box and trimap inputs. P3M-500-NP is added to public-matting evaluation. The original main-training defaults remain unchanged; newly specified prompt-sampling details alone do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Table 3c adds training-dataset controls for ZIM and Matting-Any; Table 8 tests converter post-processing and training existing models on SA1B-Matte. Figure 8 examines prompt-density sensitivity under domain shift, and Appendix C.1 reports a data-volume check. Original component, object-size, and hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The medical-IoU distribution plot is retained as Figure 15 from v1 Figure 8. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. V2's discussion of uncertain predictions does not add statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds transfer, training-control, prompt-count, and transparency results; Table 7 reports ZIM MSE 15.55 and SAD 298.78. Matched MicroMat-3K, inpainting, NVOS, and original ablation values remain unchanged, while the complete v1 AM-2K/AIM-500 table is omitted. Figure 8 plots Matte-Any's AIM-500 box MSE near 22, versus 38.497 in v1 Table 2 and about 38.5 in v2 Figure 5; the PDFs do not explain this discrepancy.

T1.justification: The matting-loss and prompt-masked-attention definitions in Equations 1–5 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that label-converted SA1B-Matte and the decoder/attention improvements enable precise micro-level zero-shot matting and downstream transfer. The principal contributions and MicroMat-3K benchmark claim remain the same; additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains the mismatch between whole-foreground public matting labels and object/part-level predictions, linking box-prompt failures to SAM ambiguity and discussing dense-point mitigation. It adds substantive transparency limitations, interprets training-data controls and frozen-backbone constraints, and explicitly acknowledges prompt ambiguity and uncertain predictions in the conclusion.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies RITM evaluation with at most 12 points, 10% box perturbation, eight V100 GPUs, and training times of seven and five days. The code-access pointer changes from a repository to a project website. Conversely, v1's explicit COCO 2017 validation/10-point inpainting setup and training-box-perturbation statement are omitted.

R1.justification: New references support transparency and fine-grained segmentation evaluations and identify components such as Grounding DINO and the inpainting model. The related-work narrative and central positioning around SAM generalization and macro-level matting datasets remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The standalone downstream-task section becomes a short Section 5.3 with detailed accounts moved to Appendix B. Appendix material is reorganized into expanded subsections, method explanations are condensed, and the conclusion is rewritten around limitations and future work. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds the multipanel transfer chart, domain-shift examples, prompt-count curves, transparency and component-transfer tables, and an expanded training-data ablation table. It removes the original public-matting table, reduces and rearranges Figures 1–2, and relocates numerous downstream figures and tables into the appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central data-versus-architecture argument through Tables 3c and 8, directly testing explanations that v1 largely supported indirectly. Its domain-shift and transparency analyses also establish important applicability limits. These gains in validation and qualification outweigh the loss of some comparison and protocol detail, although the unexplained Matte-Any discrepancy between Figures 5 and 8 weakens the public-benchmark reporting.
